title: The Golden Cycle: Icosahedral Shells, from the Chain of Karma to the Gnomon
description:
Version 2 adds Chapter 13, The Truncated Icosahedron Star (TI Star, #78): the truncated icosahedron with its own face pyramids turned outwards starts an exact doubling cycle and an exact golden cycle, with eleven solids per turn, a self-polar middle and, under the rule of Chapter 10, a four-step cycle of its own through DICTO's Star Halo; the gnomon chapter now closes the book as Chapter 14. About the author lists all four books.

A book gathering DICTO's work on icosahedral shells: thirteen papers as thirteen chapters in three parts, from the Chain of Karma (#22) to the gnomon (#54), with a new opening, a conclusion, a table of the cycles, open problems, an index and an About the author page. Version 1.1 corrects Figure 1.1 (the Lotus seed pulled apart), re-shot so that every piece lies inside the frame.

It shows five things. (1) Endless shells: the icosahedron and the dodecahedron each fill exactly as a shell round the other, and the shells alternate without end, growing by φ³ each turn (the Chain of Karma). (2) A cycle of six solids: six icosahedral solids nest exactly, each layer filled by a few repeated pieces, and the cycle repeats every φ³ in both directions (the Spheres of Dharma); the same counts close a cluster of twelve around one (the Bodhi Seed), and the stages in between pass through the DICTO Hecatodihedron. (3) Turned inside out and seeded: taking polars reverses every nesting and gives a second exact cycle; both cycles fit in one space only up to a factor 3; and DICTO's twin solids, the Hecatodihedron and the Ogdoecontahedron, seed a golden cycle that grows to twelve stations. (4) One rule that grows the shells: each corner of a solid giving the face plane of the next builds the cycle step by step and closes it exactly (Universal PiTet), runs up and down from the Ogdoecontahedron, and keeps every tower of shells nested (Kyushindo Cores). (5) The whole turn is a gnomon: the full turn of twelve stations adds exactly what makes the next icosahedron the same shape as the first.

Every solid is exact in the numbers a + b√5 with a and b rational, and every nesting and volume is checked with remainder zero. Each chapter is its paper, theorems and proofs word for word, and names the paper and DICTO DOI it comes from; sources checked for every chapter are listed in an appendix. The cover is the GOLDEN square: GOLDEN across and down a 6 × 6 square, each letter one station of the inside-out golden cycle (rhombic triacontahedron, dodecahedron, icosidodecahedron, DICTO Ogdoecontahedron, pentakis dodecahedron, icosahedron).

The ideas and names are DICTO's. Computation and proof with Claude (Anthropic). Licence CC BY-SA 4.0. More at dictospheres.com.
